#6141. United Airlines Doubles Flights On 7 Routes From Major Hub: See Full List Now

United Airlines has built an extensive network across the United States and continues to review and adjust its schedules. In its latest schedule update, the Star Alliance member has planned to double the number of flights on seven routes from Denver International Airport (DEN).

The Colorado hub is United's second-busiest in terms of passenger numbers, flights, and available seats, and the airline operates more than 500 daily flights from the airport.

According to schedule data from aviation analytics provider Cirium, United is doubling flight frequencies on routes to Syracuse Hancock International Airport (SYR), Richmond International Airport (RIC), Norfolk International Airport (ORF), Dane County Regional Airport (MSN) in Madison, and Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport (MKE) for the upcoming summer season.

All five routes had one daily flight last summer, but will see two daily services next summer. The airline is also adding one daily flight each to its routes to the Eastern Iowa Airport (CID) in Cedar Rapids and Cleveland Hopkins International Airport (CLE).

Any other airline offering flights from DEN?

*Frequency is based on the scheduled departures in June 2027.

Interestingly, the transcontinental market from both Richmond and Norfolk appears to be heating up, particularly to the West Coast. American Airlines and Delta Air Lines dominate more than half of the passenger traffic at these Virginia airports, but much of their traffic is funneled through major hubs such as Charlotte, Atlanta and Dallas/Fort Worth. For years, nonstop flights from these mid-sized Virginia airports to the West Coast were limited.

But Breeze Airways began changing that by introducing transcontinental services using its Airbus A220-300 aircraft. The low-cost carrier launched flights from Richmond to San Francisco International Airport (SFO) and Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), as well as from Norfolk to LAX and San Diego International Airport (SAN). More recently, in October, United announced plans to introduce twice-weekly flights from its San Francisco hub to both Richmond and Norfolk in spring 2027.

This will give Norfolk its first scheduled nonstop connection to the San Francisco Bay Area and put United in direct competition with Breeze on the Richmond–San Francisco route. Alaska Airlines also announced recently that it would launch daily, year-round flights between Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA) and Norfolk on June 10, 2027, using Boeing 737-900 aircraft. Notably, Seattle was Norfolk's largest unserved domestic market.

United is teaming up with Air Canada to give flyers more choices.

Elsewhere, United is continuing to expand its network from Denver, where it has several new international routes planned for summer 2027. On May 27, the airline is launching daily, year-round flights to Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport (CDG), using Boeing 787-9 aircraft. This will be its first nonstop service between Denver and Paris and its fifth European destination from the Colorado hub.

The Star Alliance member is also adding two seasonal routes to Canada. On April 29, it is starting daily flights to Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International Airport (YOW), running through October 31, 2027, as part of United's expanded joint venture with Air Canada. In addition, it is commencing Saturday-only flights to Québec City Jean Lesage International Airport (YQB), operating from May 29 through October 30, 2027.

Overall, according to Cirium schedule data, United will operate more than 500 daily flights from Denver during the summer season. Among its busiest routes are Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD), Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH), Colorado Springs Airport (COS), and Aspen/Pitkin County Airport (ASE), each seeing at least ten daily departures.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

Correction: Denver-Ottawa is slated to be daily and year-round. No tickets are bookable beyond October 2027 for any route. But according to the Denver airport and the airline the route is year-round. Quebec City is seasonal though

It’s great to see new flights from Norfolk to Denver and San Francisco on United and the announcement of Alaska’s entry with daily service between Norfolk and Seattle is a game changer. Breeze needs to get serious with year-round daily service to San Diego and Los Angeles or the legacy carriers will pick up those routes as well. What’s really missing now is American non-stop service between Norfolk and Phoenix. Come on AA, wake up!

#6140. 9 Chefs on the Meals They're Traveling For in 2027—From Korean Soups to Peruvian Ceviche

Any professional chef can confirm that while menu development, staffing, interior design, and operations are all part of running a restaurant or kitchen, finding the time to travel in search of different flavors often feels like a rare luxury. But spending time in a different city or region is key to staying inspired. Even a quick weekend getaway can lead to incorporating new ingredients in familiar dishes, serve as an opportunity to learn a new culinary technique, help forge a connection with one’s own heritage, or connect with peers who are pushing the industry forward.

As the end of the calendar year draws near, we spoke with some of our favorite women chefs about where they’re most excited to visit in 2027—from a sushi counter in Tokyo to the oldest restaurant in Beirut—and what they’re hoping to eat and learn from those travels.

A table at ARREA!, Almuerzo Otoño's restaurant in Álava, Spain

“I went [to the Basque Country] for the first time in 2013, but it was such a quick, rushed trip that I left feeling like I’d barely scratched the surface. I’ve been wanting to go back and really do it right ever since. At the top of my list of spots is Arrea!, Edorta Lamo’s restaurant in Kanpezu, a small village in the mountains of Álava. I’ve heard such wonderful things about it. What excites me is that it’s not the Basque Country most people think of first—as in, San Sebastián with its coastline and all of its pintxo bars. It’s inland cooking, built on what’s hunted, foraged, and grown right there in the mountains. And I'll be eating my way through plenty of pintxo bars too, of course. — Katie Button, chef/co-founder of Cúrate Bar de Tapas in Asheville, and author of Spanish Accent cookbook

“I’m in love with Erin French’s new cookbook [Seize the Supper], and wildly enough, Maine is one of the few states I've never been to. So, I'm plotting something for next summer. I love that it's a mostly female crew, a standout (unfortunately) in our industry. Erin’s focus on local produce and connecting to the earth speaks to my own regenerative cooking and inspires me constantly to dig deeper and deeper. I also admire her ethos of humble simplicity, distilling dishes to their core, filled with soul and properly honoring ingredients, with a nod to her family's heritage. I dream of her play on sweet and savory—like the soft polenta with honey and ricotta.” — Camilla Marcus, chef and founder of Westbourne

The seafood platter at the new Casa Juani in Boulder

Casa Juani's Spain-inspired sea urchin dish

“I am most looking forward to traveling to Boulder to visit my friends Kelly Jeun and Eduardo Vallelobo at their restaurant Casa Juani. Both are accomplished chefs who are experts in Italian and Spanish cuisines, and they recently made Bon Appétit's Best New Restaurants list. I am most excited to try everything on their menu, which is entirely Spanish. Eduardo is very proud of—and from!—Madrid, and the menu celebrates Spanish cuisine and culture.” —Melissa Rodriguez, Chef & Partner at Crane Club & Bar CC in New York City

For cookbook author Rebekah Peppler, edomae-style sushi is a must-eat in 2027.

“[Sushi Meino], a six-seat counter in Tokyo’s Azabujuban neighborhood by Chef Mei Kougo, one of only a few female sushi masters in Japan, has been high on my list since it opened in 2023 and I haven’t yet had the luck of securing a very-difficult-to-get reservation. I'm heading back to Tokyo in the spring and hoping 2027 will be my year! If I don’t get in, I’ll still be heading to Makimaki, her takeout-only hosomaki shop that opened nearby earlier this year.” — Rebekah Peppler, recipe developer and author

Baekyangsa Temple, where Buddhist nun and chef Jeong Kwan hosts meals

Freshly foraged ingredients, including mushrooms, herbs, and greens, used by chef Jeong Kwan

“Eating at venerable Jeong Kwan’s table has been high on my list for years, and I was devastated to be out of town when she and Chef Esu Lee were cooking together at his excellent restaurant Orson in Paris recently. It lit a fire in me to finally prioritize booking a trip to Baekyangsa Temple [where she cooks] to attend one of her demonstrations in 2027.” — R.P.

Street bread Ka'ak is the reason chef Mary Attea will be headed to Lebanon in 2027.

“I'm dying to try manakish and shawarma straight from the source. Plus ka'ak, the ring-shaped street bread with sesame, along with all the spreads from the market. And [I want to pay a] visit to El Soussi, one of Beirut's oldest restaurants, famous for its Lebanese breakfast, especially msabbaha, the warm mashed chickpeas with lemon and tahini. I'd be sure to get an order of beid ghanam as well, which is lambs testicles cooked in lemon and olive oil, served with fattet hummus. Growing up in the US with Lebanese heritage, we often ate many Lebanese meals as a family. But the dishes we prepared and enjoyed were such a small sliver of everything Lebanon has to offer. I've been wanting to go for such a long time so I could experience the vastness of this incredible cuisine and the country's beauty. I was meant to travel there this past March, which was postponed, so it's top of my list for 2027!” —Chef Mary Attea, executive chef of Musket Room and Raf’s in New York City

A ceviche dish at Lima restaurant Al Toke Pez

“I’m especially excited to explore Nikkei cuisine and experience Peruvian ceviche firsthand. In Mexico, we make wonderful ceviches, but I believe Peruvians have truly mastered the art of preparing this dish. I want to experience their approach to seafood, acidity, and flavor in its place of origin, while exploring the broader culinary traditions of Peru. I believe there are many shared histories and points of connection between Latin American cultures that we don’t always recognize, and I want to explore those connections through food. I’m also drawn to the opportunity to experience traditional Mesoamérican markets that are still operating throughout Peru, not only in Lima but in other regions as well. Markets reveal so much about a place: its ingredients, its people, its traditions, and the ways food connects communities. I’d also love to experience Inca culture firsthand and better understand the country’s rich cultural and culinary heritage.” —Norma Listman, chef and co-founder, Masala y Maíz in Mexico City

Traditional Assamese food items on sale at the annual Bhogali Bihu Festival in Assam

“I’m particularly interested in Assam’s distinctive use of black sesame and wild greens. During a trip to Mumbai, I had the opportunity to taste Assamese food prepared by two sisters who cook and preserve traditional Assamese foodways. Their food completely blew my mind. I would love to travel to Assam to learn more about the region’s culinary traditions and experience its food culture firsthand. As a chef who cooks both Indian and Mexican cuisine, I feel a responsibility to keep learning and exploring the vastness and richness of India’s food traditions. India is incredibly diverse, and there is still so much for me to discover. Now, as the mother of a mixed child with Indian heritage, I feel an even greater responsibility to expose him to his culture. Traveling to Assam would be an opportunity to continue learning for myself while creating a meaningful connection between my son and his cultural roots.” — N.L.

“I hosted a pop-up at ADI last year, and was able to witness firsthand the ways in which chef Kanchan [Adhikari] is doing the most incredibly inventive things with food within the South Asian diaspora while also marrying it with a Japanese omakase-style sentiment. One of my favorite restaurants of the past year and I am counting down the days until I can eat a meal in that gorgeous dining room again!"” —Samah Dada, chef and creator of recipe platform DADA Eats

A bowl of pollock soup, a dish local to Inje in South Korea

“Inje is the smallest county in South Korea and is most famous for hwangtae guk (dried pollock) soup. You can find many restaurants clustered together there that serve this regional specialty, but my absolute favorite is a place called Song-yi Sikdang. The brief menu basically comes down to the hwangtae jungsik—a set that includes pollock soup, a whole grilled pollock, an assortment of 12 perfectly seasoned namul banchans, and a warm bowl of rice. Inje is located in the Taebaek mountains alongside rivers and basins, so when you get there, you’re surrounded by stunning landscape and flora, which is absolutely gorgeous year round—ranging from verdant mountains, to golden and crimson foliage, to snowy tree tops. Inje is a short and tranquil two-hour drive from Seoul and feels similar to that of driving upstate on the Taconic from Manhattan. The geography and climate makes it the perfect environment for preparing dried pollock and also foraging for diverse wild greens and herbs (namuls), rare ones that you can only find there and are seasonally available at local farmers markets. —Clara Lee, co-author of Korean Soups and co-founder of food company Queens

I have been wanting to travel to Italy for many years, and Puglia has been top of mind. It feels like a place where food is still very much connected to the culture and deeply rooted in the abundance of the land. Since the provenance of things is our ethos, this feels particularly aligned for me. Anytime I travel (but specifically Europe). “I am really drawn to the simplicity of the cuisine. A beautiful local grilled fish with olive oil, handmade pasta, regional cheeses—these are all things that truly excite me as a chef because their beauty is in how uncomplicated they are. Local, fresh bounty, cooked well: to me this is what makes food memorable.” —Abigail Dahan-Kramer, pastry chef at Provenance in Philadelphia

As the most discerning, up-to-the-minute voice in all things travel, Condé Nast Traveler is the global citizen’s bible and muse, offering both inspiration and vital intel. We understand that time is the greatest luxury, which is why Condé Nast Traveler mines its network of experts and influencers so that you never waste a meal, a drink, or a hotel stay wherever you are in the world.

#6139. American Adds New Routes, Drops Others in Reshuffle at LAX

American Airlines will add new connections and cut others as it works to optimize its network at Los Angeles.

The carrier confirmed Friday that it will launch year-round service from LAX to Reno, Nevada, and seasonal service to Bozeman, Montana, and Grand Junction, Colorado.

LA-Reno will operate three times weekly, starting May 27, 2027, using Embraer E175 aircraft.

The routes to Bozeman and Grand Junction will operate from May 27 to Aug. 9, with Bozeman service using an E175 and Grand Junction flights using a Bombardier CRJ700.

An American official said Grand Junction is a “seasonal market addition” while service to Aspen/Pitkin County, Colorado, is temporarily suspended due to construction work there.

American will also add frequencies on some existing routes out of LAX next summer:

The carrier also confirmed that it will drop service from Los Angeles to Cleveland and Des Moines, Iowa, on February 11.

As the holidays inch closer, many of you might be wondering what to get for people on your gift list. As a travel expert who’s constantly on the go, I will say some of my favorite things revolve around staying organized and being comfortable — from luggage to passports, I always know where my essentials are, and now that I travel with my kids, it’s even more important.

I’m sharing a few of my favorite things that also make great gift ideas for friends and family.

My favorite, which I’ll always throw in my bag, is my Bose QuietComfort noise-canceling headphones. These are stylish and have great sound quality — the surround sound is awesome. They are my go-to for flights; they are comfortable and connect seamlessly via Bluetooth.

TPG tip: Bose is often on sale during Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale. Make sure you stack any deals with a card that earns rewards on Amazon purchases.

Best for: Getting things done on the go without a laptop

Perfect for loading up movies and shows I might want to watch on the plane or loading up a few movies for the kids so I don’t have to rely on inflight entertainment. I also don’t love traveling with a laptop, so this is a great option for me to keep up with work on the go.

TPG Tip: Keep an eye out for Apple's "today only" promotions that offer larger-than-normal points-earning opportunities. Shopping portals are another great way to stack earnings on top of credit card rewards.

Best for: Anyone who ever checks a bag at the airport

You know I’m always a fan of Apple AirTags because there are plenty of times I need to check a bag when traveling with my family (but they are great for backpacks, purses and more). Plus, if your bag is ever lost, multiple airlines now allow you to share your AirTag location.

TPG tip: Amazon routinely offers sales on AirTags during Black Friday. You can stack your savings if you have the Amazon Prime Visa or look for targeted shopping offers you can activate on your credit cards.

Best for: Staying connected with friends and family abroad

I use this eSIM when traveling overseas — it’s $50 per month for unlimited international data and calling and works in over 165 countries.

TPG tip: Limited-time plans are also available if you need to stay connected for shorter trips.

Best for: Anyone who doesn’t want to juggle multiple adapters and chargers

This charger doubles as an adapter that works in over 200 countries, so you never have to worry about your devices. Fits securely in any socket for seamless charging of up to four devices.

TPG tip: Anker always runs an annual Black Friday sale on both its site and Amazon. If you have a card that’s good for Amazon, you can stack your savings and your credit card rewards.

Best for: Giving the gift of peace of mind

Safety is so important when I travel — especially if my kids are with me. The Kidde carbon monoxide detector is lightweight, battery-operated and fits easily in my bag. Just remember to pop out the batteries before going through airport security.

TPG tip: Make sure you’re using a card that’s great for Amazon to maximize your purchase.

Best for: The traveling family with both Apple and Google devices

The world’s first trackable suitcase from Melbourne, Australia-based luggage brand July. I have tested it out on several trips, and I love the spinning double wheels, its lightweight polycarbonate shell and lifetime warranty. The tracking works with both Apple and Google devices — it's easy to set up the tracking on your phone. Prices range from $325 to $395, depending on features.

TPG tip: July is currently offering 20% off the full range, sitewide, no minimum spend. Ends Nov. 29.

Best for: Anyone who wants to skip the line at the airport

Use the membership credits on your credit card to gift membership to others if you already have it! There are several credit cards that offer Global Entry credits and a few more that offer Clear credits as a benefit. If you hold a certain elite status on Delta Air Lines or United Global Services, you can also receive complimentary Clear membership.

TPG tip: If you have multiple cards with Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credits, you can use one of them to gift a membership to a friend or family member.

Sign up for Clear with TPG's special offer: $40 off your first year of membership and a free booking of Clear Concierge (valued at $99).

These plane art pieces by Pop Art Prince and Scout Design Studio are so unique and look great in my home office. If you have an AvGeek in your life, these might just make the perfect gift for their home or office.

TPG tip: Etsy is a shop on Rakuten, and you can stack your credit card rewards with the portal for even more savings.

Best for: Bringing your favorite destination home with you

I love these scents — the candles are 100% soy wax with a 65-hour burn time. I am currently burning Paris Nuit and Holiday in my home — they bring the chic smell of hotels right to you. Created by my friend, fellow travel content creator Lindsay Silberman.

Best for: Travelers who run hot on long-haul flights

I run hot on planes, so I opt for these Lululemon shorts. They keep me comfortable even when I'm sleeping in transit (a must-have for my travel day clothes), and they come in multiple colors. Given my height, it's also a plus that they come in multiple inseam lengths.

Their long-sleeve Metal Vent Tech Long-Sleeve Shirt is lightweight and sweat-wicking — another travel day fav of mine.

TPG tip: I save on them by using my quarterly $75 Lululemon statement credit on my (enrollment required).

Bombas compression socks are a must for long-haul flights to help ward off deep vein thrombosis (DVT), aka blood clots, which can occur from reduced circulation and sitting for too long. I always pack my Bombas compression socks (3-pack, $91.50) and stay well-hydrated on flights.

TPG tip: Purchase using Rove’s shopping portal and earn up to 6x Rove miles.

You can stack rewards and double dip (or even triple dip) and earn your credit card points and miles on purchases, plus airline miles or other currencies when you do your online shopping via portals. I like to earn Amex points with Rakuten or Rove Miles through Rove.

This is three times more than the standard referral offer!
